title: The Framework Gap
briefing: Internal Audit has rated the risk management framework 'needs improvement'. Findings: registers are kept differently in each business unit, risks are rarely re-assessed, and the Risk Committee sees 140 risks with no prioritisation.
You have to respond to the audit and fix it.

context.text: Audit also noted that a known appetite breach was missing from a committee report. This finding is about you.
Audit credited the new appetite cascade as the framework's strongest element.

evidence.title: Internal Audit report (summary)
body: F1: Five business units use five register formats and scales. F2: 58% of risks have not been reviewed in over 12 months. F3: The Risk Committee receives all 140 risks with no ranking. F4: Three risks have no named owner.

evidence.title: Framework team capacity
evidence.body: You plus half of Lina's time. A register system licence costs 55,000 a year; a spreadsheet standard costs nothing but time.

questions.prompt: What is the root cause behind F1 to F4?

options.label: No single standard (method, scales, review cycle, ownership) set and enforced by the second line
options.feedback: Each finding is a symptom of the missing standard.

options.label: Business units don't care about risk
options.feedback: Blame without a cause; units fill a vacuum the framework left.

options.label: No register software
options.feedback: A tool helps but would just automate five different methods.

questions.prompt: Which management response do you commit to?

options.label: Agree each finding; one method and scale by month 2, owners named immediately, quarterly reviews from month 3, top-15 view to committee from next meeting
options.feedback: Specific, sequenced and realistic for your capacity.

options.label: Dispute F2: many risks don't change
options.feedback: Arguing with evidence weakens credibility; agree and fix.

options.label: Commit to fixing all findings in 30 days
options.feedback: Over-promising with half a team guarantees a follow-up finding.

questions.prompt: How should the committee's top risks be chosen?

options.label: Rank by residual rating against appetite, plus risks to strategic objectives, with the full register available on request
options.feedback: Focuses the committee where decisions are needed.

options.label: The 15 largest inherent risks
options.feedback: Inherent ratings ignore controls already working.

options.label: Three risks from each business unit

questions.prompt: Buy the 55,000-a-year register system now? Your authority is 300,000.

options.label: Not yet: standardise the method in a shared template first, then choose a system that fits it next year
options.feedback: Fix the process before automating it.

options.label: Buy it now: software will force consistency
options.feedback: Within authority, but tools don't fix an undefined method.

options.label: Never: spreadsheets are fine forever
options.feedback: Fine for now; not forever at 140 risks and growing.

questions.prompt: How do you present the response to the Audit Committee?

options.label: Own the findings openly, present the plan and dates, and offer progress reporting each quarter
options.feedback: Ownership plus a plan rebuilds confidence.

options.label: Explain why each finding happened
options.feedback: Explanations without a plan sound like excuses.

options.label: Ask Internal Audit to present it
options.feedback: Management responds to audit, not the other way round.

lesson: Audit findings usually share a root cause. Agree, fix the standard before the tool, prioritise for the committee, and report progress until closed.
